# Robust closure from an actual inner endpoint triangle

This is a conditional planar three-fiber theorem. It extends the full
canonical triangular endpoint case to convex endpoints containing a
specified inner triangle, even when their actual outer supporting facets
are arbitrarily short. No outer facet-length stability is asserted.

## 1. Statement

Let

    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1),
    T={x:v_i.x<=1 for i=1,2,3},       |T|=9/2,
    eta_*=2-sqrt(33)/3.

One has 1/12<eta_*<1. Let A,K,B be the only nonempty integer fibers,
at -1,0,1 respectively, of an actual convex body. Assume they are
full planar convex bodies, so (A+B)/2 subset K. Suppose 0 lies in
int K and every ambient halfspace

    H_i={(z,x):v_i.x>=z}

attains the genuine raw mixed depth Q at (0,0). Assume every A cut
v_i.x=-1 is proper and

    (1-eta)T subset B subset T,
    0<=eta<=eta_*.                                  (1)

Put a=|A|,k=|K|,b=|B|,M=a+k+b. If B is nonheavy, meaning

    b<=a+k,                                        (2)

then the original source satisfies

    Q>(2/9)M.                                      (3)

If b>a+k, the ordinary centroid in the B fiber has raw mixed depth
at least (4/9)b>(2/9)M. This alternative supplies an actual point,
without asserting the same guarantee for the original source. No
global depth-maximizer hypothesis is imposed.

A convenient sufficient version of (1) is eta<=1/12. Accordingly,
the same existence conclusion holds if B subset T and

    |T\B|<|T|/324,                                 (4)

with all the other cap hypotheses unchanged. The source guarantee
in (3) retains the nonheavy qualification (2).

## 2. The original cap profiles force a high A point

Assume (2) and, for contradiction, Q<=2M/9. All three B captures
have zero area because B subset T. Write the captured A areas in
increasing order as u<=v<=w, and put

    F=u+v+w/4,
    delta=a-u-v.

The A traces cover the plane: their normals sum to zero and their
thresholds are all -1. The K traces also cover the plane, with
thresholds 0. The ordinary positive-part cap-cover inequality says

    |L|<=sum_i(c_i-alpha)_+ +(9/4)alpha              (5)

for a planar body L covered by caps of areas c_i and every alpha>=0.
A complete proof is Section 3 of
`candidate cce182d75ffe5c52`.
For clarity, sequentially trim deeper parallel caps until each retained
cap area is at most alpha. Each removal is at most (c_i-alpha)_+.
If the retained set has positive area, one covering cap contains its
centroid and ordinary Grünbaum bounds the retained area by9alpha/4;
if it has zero area, the removal bound already proves (5). Cap-area
continuity justifies each chosen parallel threshold, including the
zero-volume stopping case.

Apply (5) to A with alpha=u and to K with alpha=Q-w. The latter
threshold is nonnegative because the middle volume Q-w is positive.
The middle cap volumes are Q-u,Q-v,Q-w. This gives

    a<=w+v+u/4,             delta<=w,
    k<=(9/4)Q-F.                                  (6)

The bad target and the middle profile imply

    k<=a+b-2F,
    Q<=(4/9)(a+b-F).                              (7)

For the first relation, substitute (9/4)Q<=M/2 into (6). For the
second, substitute k<=(9/4)Q-F into Q<=2(a+b+k)/9 and rearrange.
Combining the first relation with b<=a+k forces F<=a. Thus

    delta=a-u-v>=w/4>0,                           (8)

where w>0 follows from the proper A cuts.

The union of the two smaller A caps has area at most u+v<a, so
there is a point simultaneously strictly missing those two caps.
If i,j are their normal indices and l indexes the largest cap, then

    v_i.x<-1, v_j.x<-1,
    v_l.x=-v_i.x-v_j.x>2.

Consequently

    h=h_A(v_l)>2,
    H=h+1>3.                                     (9)

This support-height conclusion uses the original, unshifted caps.
Meanwhile delta<=w and b<=|T|=9/2 give the bad-target upper bound

    Q<=(4/9)(b+delta-w/4)<=4b/9+w/3<=2+w/3.        (10)

## 3. A cap homothety controls the shifted A volume exactly

Let

    D=A intersect {x:v_l.x>=-1},      |D|=w,
    A_eta=A intersect {x:v_l.x>=-1+eta},
    w_eta=|A_eta|.

Choose p in A attaining v_l.p=h. For

    theta=1-eta/H,

the homothety p+theta(D-p) is contained in A by convexity. Its
minimum v_l-coordinate is

    h+theta(-1-h)=-1+eta.

Thus this whole homothetic copy of D lies in A_eta. Since H>3 and
0<=eta<1, it follows that

    w_eta >= (1-eta/H)^2 w
             >= (1-eta/3)^2 w.                    (11)

All sets in this assertion are actual portions of A. It is not a
comparison with a replacement fiber or with an independently selected
cap. The shifted cut is proper because the original cut was proper
and h>2.

## 4. An inner B facet produces the required middle volume

Let F_eta be the facet of (1-eta)T on v_l.x=1-eta. It is an actual
segment contained in B and has length

    |F_eta|_1=3(1-eta)|v_l|.

Every point of (A_eta+F_eta)/2 belongs to K by compatibility and
has v_l-coordinate at least

    [(-1+eta)+(1-eta)]/2=0.

It therefore lies in the original unshifted middle cap. Addition of
a segment to a planar convex body has exact area equal to body area
plus segment length times perpendicular projection width. Indeed each
nonempty parallel slice is an interval whose length is increased by
the segment length, and one integrates those slice lengths over the
perpendicular projection. Here the projection width is
(H-eta)/|v_l|, so

    |A_eta+F_eta|=w_eta+3(1-eta)(H-eta).             (12)

The original A contribution is still w. Its total critical mass is
therefore

    Q >= w+[w_eta+3(1-eta)(H-eta)]/4
      > [1+(1/4)(1-eta/3)^2]w
                    +(3/4)(1-eta)(3-eta),          (13)

using (9), (11), and eta<1. In particular the strictness comes from
the actual height H>3, not an approximation of a supporting facet.
Subtract the right side of (10) from the lower expression in (13):

    [2/3+(1/4)(1-eta/3)^2]w
                     +1/4-3eta+(3/4)eta^2.         (14)

The constant polynomial is nonnegative for 0<=eta<=eta_*; its
smaller root is exactly 2-sqrt(33)/3. Its w coefficient is positive,
and w>0. Hence (14) is strictly positive throughout the stated closed
range, including eta=eta_*. This contradicts (10), proving (3).

For the simpler range eta<=1/12, the constant term in (14) is at
least 1/192: its derivative -3+(3/2)eta is negative there, and its
value at 1/12 is 1/192. This supplies an explicit strict margin in
the contradictory pair of cap bounds. No radius or strip-area loss
estimate is needed for this argument.

## 5. Missing volume forces an actual homothetic core

Let L be any d-dimensional convex body with centroid g, and let B
be a compact convex subset of L. For 0<eta<1, if

    |L\B|<Gamma_d eta^d |L|,
    Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d,

then

    (1-eta)L+eta g subset B.                       (15)

Indeed any point x of the left side has the form x=(1-eta)p+eta g
for p in L. The body L_x=(1-eta)p+eta L is contained in L by
convexity, has centroid x, and has volume eta^d|L|. If x were outside
B, strict separation would supply a closed halfspace containing x and
disjoint from B. Ordinary Grünbaum at the centroid of L_x would put
at least Gamma_d eta^d|L| of L outside B, contradicting the strict
missing-volume assumption. This proves (15).

Apply this to the planar centroid-zero triangle T with eta=1/12.
Then

    Gamma_2 eta^2=(4/9)(1/12)^2=1/324.

Thus (4) implies (1), and the theorem already proved applies. The
stronger explicit missing-volume threshold Gamma_2 eta_*^2 would
also suffice. None of these implications controls, or needs to
control, the lengths of the actual outer supporting facets of B.

## Scope

The hypotheses retain the actual three-fiber geometry, all three
proper A cuts, genuine all-ambient depth criticality, and the inner
triangle assumption. When B is nonheavy the guarantee belongs to the
original deterministic middle-fiber source. If B is heavy, its actual
ordinary centroid is used. The asserted halfspace inequalities refer
to every closed ambient halfspace through those points, not just the
three displayed normals.

The continuous coordinates remain in the canonical triangle frame
throughout. No integer coordinate is transformed or rounded. All
measures are the actual planar areas of the original fibers, and no
global depth-maximizer assumption is required. The inner core condition
is explicit and is not asserted for arbitrary B.
